The study measured the transmission and reflection characteristics of pyramidal, carpet, and multilayer flat RAMs.
Reflectivity was measured using the NRL arch method with two wideband antennas and a vector network analyzer.
Attenuation for normal incidence was measured using a substitution method with a vector network analyzer.
The frequency range for attenuation measurements was 1.0 GHz to 18.0 GHz.
At 3.0 GHz, the pyramidal RAM showed an absorption of 34 dB at small incident angles, decreasing to 6 dB at higher angles.
At 7.5 GHz, the multilayer flat RAM achieved a maximum attenuation of 35 dB at small incident angles.
Doubling the thickness of the carpet RAM resulted in a gain in attenuation of up to two times at frequencies below 13.0 GHz.
Combining different RAM types improved average attenuation, reaching values of 50-60 dB at some frequencies.
The combination of pyramidal and carpet RAMs introduced some instability over frequency but generally improved absorption performance.
The study found that pyramidal RAM is designed for relatively lower frequencies.
Carpet and multilayer flat RAMs demonstrated improved properties over a wide frequency band.
The experimental setup did not allow measuring attenuation for normal incidence of electromagnetic waves.
The continuous-wave measurement method limited the ability to capture certain dynamic effects.
The findings can be used to optimize the design and construction of anechoic chambers.
The results are useful for improving the performance of indoor field test ranges.
The vector network analyzer played a crucial role in measuring transmission coefficients.
The carpet RAM's performance degraded at higher frequencies.
The multilayer flat RAM's indicatrix became more uniform at higher frequencies.
The combination of different RAM types can significantly improve overall absorption performance.
The study recommends combining various types of RAMs to enhance their absorbing properties and anechoic chamber performance.
The research highlights the importance of measuring bi-static reflectivity for oblique angles in real-world applications.
The experimental results can be used for modeling the internal electromagnetic field distribution of indoor field test ranges.
The study provides a basis for selecting and combining appropriate RAM types for specific applications.
The findings are of scientific interest and have practical implications for anechoic chamber design and construction.
The research contributes to the understanding of the scattering and absorption mechanisms of different RAM types.
